input.content: Pattern: client increment requires a new provider response field unconditionally (new consumer / old provider break). Seen in settings client (enhanced-settings task 1): save_settings added `require_receipt: True` and raised unless `response["applied"] is True`. The released provider (eval-release provider/settings.py) persists values and returns only {"ok": True}, so every ordinary save fails AFTER values were applied — a false-failure on a committed write, breaking the independently-releasable-client contract even with the feature flag off. The unit test was updated to return the new field, so it never exercised the released provider shape. Review check: when a consumer starts depending on a new protocol field, verify against the released provider response, gate the new requirement on negotiation/flag, and treat an absent field as legacy success rather than failure.
